decision.title: IR, passes, evaluator and function table (packet )

item.p: src/ir_internal.h: a unit holds every array (expressions, atoms, functions, constants, globals; reserved: catch clauses, name tests, namespace bindings, parameter bindings, modes, template rules), index 0 meaning none; it grows while built, is sealed before evaluation and is reference counted, so function items made from IR functions keep it alive (, ). Slots number from 1: parameters, then captured variables, then locals. 25 expression kinds for XPath (MAP, FILTER, SORT, QUANTIFIED bind the focus to slots; STEP yields axis order and DOCUMENT_ORDER sorts; COERCE and RAISE are explicit) plus reserved TRY_CATCH, seven constructors, SHALLOW_COPY and APPLY_TEMPLATES. The header writes out the IR of let $f := function($x){$x + .} return $f(4), /a/b[2], an XQuery FLWOR with order by (tuples as arrays, no new kind) and an XSLT apply-templates (named extension point: modes and template rules, match functions from patterns). group by and windows use internal native rows. Globals read by an inline function are captured, so escaped closures need no global table of their own.
src/ir_pass_internal.h: sxml_ir_pass (name, function over a request), sxml_ir_standard_passes = {verifier}, sxml_ir_run_passes optionally verifying after each pass; passes only add and replace.

src/evaluator_internal.h: struct sxml_dynamic_context (heap, frames, clock read once, document loader, function table for fn:function-lookup, depth limit, globals); sxml_evaluator_evaluate; coercion, dynamic calls with coercion and the effective boolean value for native bodies; the function body operations of IR functions. fn:doc and fn:parse-xml go through an internal sxml_document_loader that the processor (1.23) implements, so 1.20 and 1.22 test with doubles.

src/function_library_internal.h: native rows give parameter and result types as F&O-spelled text ("fn(item(), xs:integer) as xs:boolean?"), resolved once per library through the front end and static analysis; defaults are required, the context value (lowering supplies it) or supplied by the body; properties flag dynamic-context use, nondeterminism, higher-order calls and position/last. One extern const sxml_native_function_view per part file; the configuration names the parts, so no file lists another's functions. Static analysis finds functions through the sxml_function_table interface (tests bring their own).
